intelligence.human_view: The question was "what's 10-star service?" and the answer is in the standard he had already set, applied to the places it had not reached yet. The bottom icons are the standard — obsidian, white glyph, own colour, real object, lit on hover — and the top-right buttons fail it, because a dot is not an icon: a dot says nothing, and a button that says nothing is a button nobody can read. The fix is not a new design, it is the standard applied: a cap or open book for Academy, a star or laurel for Masterclass, a bolt for the Fast Action Club, each built to the same level as the bottom icons, each drawn from the icon library — because these are the citizen's morphing buttons, and the library is where their icons live. The cover and the feed photos are the same lesson applied to images: a photo should keep its own shape, never a forced crop. The cover gets a named size — 1920×600, 16:5 — shown in the upload flow, so the citizen knows what to bring; a drag-to-frame editor, so the citizen places it; and a library with a new special cover every month, so the cover is a real object that changes, not a rectangle that sits. The feed photo gets its shape respected — 4:5 portrait as the hero on phone, because it fills the screen and stands apart from the 16:9-everywhere crowd; 16:9 for video and landscape; 1:1 square — plus a simple editor in the composer, crop and frame and rotate, not Photoshop. The scorecard's last line is the discipline: numbers that add up, or the page says honestly what they are. A page that speaks one language — obsidian, white glyphs, own colours, elevated boards, real objects — is a page a stranger can read in two seconds. That is the standard, and tonight it reached the top-right corner, the cover, and the feed.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine your buttons all have real pictures on them — a little graduation hat, a shiny star, a lightning bolt — so you always know what they do! And your photos never get squished or cut — they keep their own shape, like magic frames that fit them perfectly!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like every button having a proper little picture, love — so you can tell at a glance what it does, instead of a tiny dot that says nothing. And your photos keep their own shape, never chopped or squished, with a simple little editor to straighten them. The cover gets a proper size, so you know what photo to bring.
intelligence.naya_view: I give every button a real icon that says what it is — no dot-only buttons anywhere — built to the level of the bottom icons. I let every photo keep its own shape, and I name the cover's size, so the citizen always knows what to bring.
